root_cause.text: A copy-paste error in the USB audio validation table caused the UAC3 AC header descriptor validator to be registered with the incorrect protocol version (UAC_VERSION_2 instead of UAC_VERSION_3), so UAC3 devices bypassed header validation entirely, allowing a malicious device with a truncated descriptor to trigger out-of-bounds reads.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff changes `FIXED(UAC_VERSION_2, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor)` to `FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor)`, and the commit message states: "The entry of the validators table for UAC3 AC header descriptor is defined with the wrong protocol version UAC_VERSION_2, while it should have been UAC_VERSION_3. This results in the validator never matching for actual UAC3 devices, causing their header descriptors to bypass validation entirely."
